candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity: recognize changes in psychosocial functioning, assess clients experiencing stress or mental-health symptoms, provide therapeutic support, and facilitate appropriate referrals.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — recognition of childbirth-related PTSD and referral for assessment/support
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize persistent trauma-specific intrusion, avoidance, and hyperarousal symptoms after a traumatic birth as possible childbirth-related PTSD and facilitate timely mental health assessment and support without confusing the presentation with postpartum blues or psychosis.

options.A: The pattern is consistent with possible childbirth-related posttraumatic stress disorder and warrants further mental health assessment and support.
options.B: The symptoms represent uncomplicated postpartum blues and require only reassurance because trauma-focused assessment would be unnecessary.
options.C: The symptoms establish postpartum psychosis because any severe distress after birth indicates impaired reality testing.
options.D: The symptoms are an expected response to emergency delivery and should not be assessed unless they persist beyond the first postpartum year.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. ACOG recognizes that a traumatic birth experience can result in postpartum posttraumatic stress disorder and recommends attention to psychological well-being as part of postpartum care. The client's recurrent intrusive memories/nightmares, avoidance of trauma reminders, hyperarousal/startle symptoms, persistence beyond one month, distress, and functional interference match major PTSD symptom domains and warrant further assessment rather than dismissal. B is incorrect because postpartum blues does not adequately explain this persistent trauma-specific pattern. C is incorrect because postpartum psychosis involves severe disturbance in reality testing such as delusions or hallucinations; those findings are not present here. D is incorrect because clinically significant trauma symptoms should be addressed when identified rather than deferred for months. A screening result or symptom pattern does not by itself replace a formal diagnostic evaluation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Traumatic childbirth can be followed by postpartum PTSD; persistent intrusion, avoidance and hyperarousal symptoms lasting beyond one month and causing functional impairment should prompt further mental health assessment and support rather than routine reassurance.
candidate.source_document_title: Optimizing Postpartum Care; Implementing Perinatal Mental Health Screening; PTSD Basics / PTSD and DSM-5
candidate.source_locator: ACOG Optimizing Postpartum Care — Comprehensive Postpartum Visit: traumatic birth experience can cause postpartum PTSD and postpartum care should assess psychological well-being. ACOG Implementing Perinatal Mental Health Screening — screening tools include PTSD instruments and all perinatal patients should receive mental-health screening. VA National Center for PTSD, PTSD Basics/PTSD and DSM-5: symptom domains include intrusion/re-experiencing, avoidance, negative cognition/mood, and hyperarousal; PTSD requires symptoms lasting more than one month with clinically significant distress or functional impairment.
